source_review.notes: Checked current AWS Builders' Library retry/backoff/idempotency guidance, AWS Well-Architected retry control and SDK retry behavior, Google SRE overload/cascading-failure guidance, and current gRPC/Envoy documentation for deadlines, retries, circuit breaking and overload control. Exact library/product configuration remains explicitly qualified.

evidence: Checked original/attempt rate, layered attempts, fan-out, hedging, deadline, remaining time, timeout, bulkhead, retry token and goodput notation.
Checked multiplicative bounds and load/retry feedback equation dimensions and qualifications.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Operation, attempt, deepest call and terminal outcome remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed executable 3 cubed = 27 layered attempts, times four = 108 calls, versus three and 12 for one owner.
Recomputed fixed 900 ms trace: attempts end at 250 and 600 ms; after 200 ms second backoff, a third would end at 1,050 ms, so two fit.
Recomputed Example 1 3 to the fourth = 81 and times five = 405; one owner three times five = 15.
Recomputed Exercise 1 3 to the fifth = 243 and times six = 1,458; Exercise 2 permits two attempts before 1,100 ms work limit.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Worst-case bounds omit cancellation/short-circuiting and are not expected-traffic predictions.

evidence: Verified nested independent attempt loops produce a product bound and fan-out/hedging multiply the deepest branch bound.
Verified one owner removes nested retry factors and absolute-deadline feasibility is lost if relative timeouts reset.
Checked retry-load feedback equation as an implicit workload model, not a stability theorem.
Verified local rejection/business outcome counterexamples invalidate indiscriminate dependency-breaker accounting.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Stability, capacity and goodput claims remain conditional/empirical because workload costs, correlations and controller delays vary.

evidence: Reviewed hidden SDK/proxy retries, deadline equality/reserve, ambiguity, non-idempotent effects, overload/permanent errors and held permits.
Reviewed shard/global breaker scope, local rejection poisoning, half-open herds, unbounded queues, fallback/shared dependencies, cache stampede, region failover and durable retry waves.
Reviewed cold recovery, telemetry/control-plane failure, stale configuration and high-stakes actuation uncertainty.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Actual safe thresholds, timeouts, capacity, retry usefulness and recovery headroom require load/fault evidence.

evidence: Traced stable identity/deadline, one retry authority, eligibility/tokens, released permits, finite queues/capacity, scoped breaker evidence, isolated probes, retry disposition, ambiguity handling and ramped recovery throughout.
Confirmed every mechanism is tied to its protected resource/failure scope and end-to-end terminal accounting.
invariant_checking.notes: Individual pattern activation is explicitly rejected as a sufficient reliability oracle.

evidence: Reviewed multiplicative, deadline-feasibility, capacity-safety, retry-stability, effect-safety, breaker-validity and recovery-safety arguments against stated premises.
Confirmed counterexamples for reset timeouts, unlimited idempotent retries, breaker-as-capacity, semaphore-behind-unbounded-queue, fallback-as-availability and failover-as-capacity.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof of a real feedback controller, production stability, universal fault independence, goodput or high-stakes safety is claimed.

evidence: Audited bound, stability, safe, idempotent, rollback, available, healthy, recovery, authoritative and success language.
Confirmed worst-case mathematics, conditional mechanism arguments, empirical evidence and named human review are separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter models composition as feedback and does not claim patterns automatically compose.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/SEPAT-090/report.json
Reproduced layered/single-owner multiplication and fixed deadline feasibility using Python 3.
Confirmed no concurrency, queue, probability, jitter, breaker, network, retry, effect or goodput behavior was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter composes resilience mechanisms through one operation identity/deadline, explicit ownership/budgets, scoped signals and end-to-end outcome rather than listing patterns independently.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers attempt trees, feedback, retry ownership, mechanism ordering/scope, half-open/recovery, queues, shedding, fallbacks/failover, durable work, observability and interaction testing.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with formal bounds, executable arithmetic, ten distinct composition cases and five exercises progressing from calculation through deadline derivation, diagnosis, backlog recovery and high-stakes transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
